title: Private Testing of Separated CATE Fibers under Unknown Propensity
banked_reason: The proposed log-free full-class pure-DP frontier is not delivered: the nuisance-independent full-fiber score construction, dense occupancy, and matched full-class estimator remain open; the sound contribution is an incremental sparse signed-family pair test.
gap_reasons: The proposed log-free full-class pure-DP frontier is not delivered: this node leaves the required nuisance-independent full-fiber score construction open, so the explicit signed-subclass pair test cannot yet supply the promised full-class estimator or R_DP equivalence.
Dense occupancy and the full-class target-fiber lift remain open.
proof_attempt_summary: The run first attempted a one-record target-fiber selector, but an exact convex-hull identity obstructed affine separation, so it pivoted to higher-order occupancy-normalized pair scores. It derived and audited a sensitivity-8/3 pure-DP test for a legal smooth signed binary family in the sparse-occupancy regime, including the relevant compatibility elbow. The field headline collapsed because dense occupancy, nuisance-cardinality-independent full-fiber scores, a total full-class estimator, and matching same-class bounds remain precisely the unresolved central theorem.
tldr: Unknown propensity can make separated pointwise CATE fibers have identical one-record nuisance mixtures while leaving an exact two-record signal. On a smooth signed binary family inside the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder class, clipping the transformed outcome preserves every signed-family moment and makes the occupancy-normalized pair score valid on all bounded-outcome datasets. Its replacement sensitivity is at most \(8/3\), and adding \(\operatorname{Laplace}(8/(3\epsilon))\) noise gives signed-family error \(C\exp(-ckp_2a^2b^2)+C\exp(-c\epsilon kp_2ab)\) without a nuisance-cardinality logarithm. This radius conclusion is limited to sparse occupancy: because \(v\asymp\ell^d\), it requires \(n\delta^{d/q}\lesssim1\). At \(\delta=r_F\) this entails \(\epsilon\gtrsim n^{-1+q/d+q/\gamma}\), and at \(\delta=r_{\mathrm{pair}}\) it requires \(d\ge2q+qd/\gamma\), with strict inequality needed to accommodate every fixed enlargement of the separation constant. Dense occupancy and the full-class target-fiber lift remain open.
gap: Simple private tests use additive one-record likelihood increments, while generic private selection and T-mechanisms control finite covers through cardinality terms. The coupled CATE fibers here have intersecting one-record convex hulls, and the published results do not supply a nuisance-independent second-order score certificate for them.
fill: The project constructs and audits the pair test on a legal smooth two-fiber family, proves an explicit pure-private test and risk bound, gives an exact finite experiment, and reduces the full-class lift to one precisely defined weighted shell functional.
